title: What the assistant was given — contract

steps.path: Chat → the line at the top of the conversation → Details
steps.headline: This is what done means for the panel that shows what the assistant was given.

rows.statement: The panel is built from the same dialog pieces as the app's other settings dialogs, not its own look.
The header shows the title, one short line beneath it, and a close cross at the right, above a hairline.
When something was left out, one line on Overview says so and opens to the full explanation.
Sections are introduced by small uppercase labels rather than cards carrying headings of their own.
Each item is a rounded row with a chevron, spaced exactly like the rows in the Preferences dialog.
Model, context window and what was given sit as three plain rows under THIS CHAT, each value on the right.
There is no footer button; Assistant settings sits at the bottom of Overview as a row with a chevron.
Quoted file text sits on the app's deepest surface behind a hairline, at the app's small caption size.
The What it got and What was cut switch is the app's own tab control, and Open is its small row button.
When nothing was left out, the same restyled panel appears in its green everything-fit state.
In the green state one green-dot line sits below the tabs, in place of the warning.
With nothing cut there is no list of cuts, only the three facts and the settings row.
The tabs come first, above the warning line and above the green everything-fit line.
The warning line shows only on Overview and is gone on the other four tabs.
File and skill text is shown as formatted text through the app's own reader, not as raw source.
The What it got and What was cut switch spans the full width of the panel.
Each side of that switch says roughly how much text it holds, so the size is obvious.
Each tool is a full-width row that opens in place, with a plain sentence saying what it does.
The switch and its text sit in one card with the skill or file they belong to.
In a chat where nothing was cut, skills that fit show their text too.
The second tab is called System.
rows.note: we should make this tab include both preset instructions and general system instructions. i want to be fully transparent about what models load in with

rows.statement: Cut text is shown side by side: red for what was cut, green for the shorter version, with line numbers.
Every chat carries one line above the conversation saying what the assistant started with.
rows.threshold: the line appears in a dev instance
rows.note: i think we can improve this a bit to match app styling a bit better. remove the checkmark. improve the button.

rows.statement: That line turns amber when the model was small and some rules or skills were left out.
Details on that line opens the panel.
The line stays for the whole conversation, so it is always the way back in.
The panel never opens by itself; the line above the conversation is the only way in.
rows.threshold: no panel opens unasked in a dev instance
rows.note: but the strip should have a warning state if stuff was cut

rows.statement: A chat given nothing extra still shows the line, saying nothing extra was given.
Open beside a file opens that file in YouCoded, exactly as pressing a file path in a chat does.
On a narrow screen the five tabs scroll sideways, so no tab label is ever cut in half.
The panel's words stand as approved: title, warning sentence, list of what was left out, tab names, tab openers.
rows.note: He kept the words and asked for seven changes in the same breath; those became rows R3, R13 to R19 after he approved them.
